_comment: AUTHORITATIVE tracker beacon contract. Each entry is the exact, sorted set of property names the tracker JS emits for that event_type after the full send pipeline (manageState -> globals -> defaults). This file is the single source of truth shared by the JS and PHP test layers: tests/js/BeaconContract.test.js asserts the tracker still emits exactly these keys (catches tracker-side renames/drops), and the PHP ingestion tests assert every handler-consumed field is present here (catches server-side drift). Regenerate with tests/js/BeaconContract.test.js when the tracker legitimately changes, and review the matching handler when a name changes. Note on the session flags, which have three different lifetimes and are NOT interchangeable: is_new_session_start marks the one REQUEST that created the session -- it rides exactly one beacon and is what a server deciding create-vs-update must branch on; is_new_session is PAGE scoped and rides every beacon originating from the page the session started on, which is what the is_entry_page dimension needs; is_new_visitor is SESSION scoped and rides every beacon of the visitor's first session, which is what keeps is_repeat_visitor from flipping mid-session; and is_new_visitor_created marks the one REQUEST that minted the visitor, the counterpart to is_new_session_start. Nothing consumes is_new_visitor_created yet -- it is there so v2 can raise a first_visit event from the request that actually created the visitor (GA does this with its _fv flag). Do not drop it as unused. A beacon from an already-active session carries none of the four. Two further session fields appear only when a new session SUCCEEDED an earlier one, so they are in none of these contracts, all of which are first-ever sessions from a cold state: prior_session_id, and time_since_last_session -- the gap to the previous session, measured by the TRACKER as a duration and sent, because the server computing it from its own clock minus the browser's was wrong by the visitor's skew and could go negative. The 'base.page_request' entry is a direct (no-referrer, no-campaign) new-session pageview. 'base.page_request.referral' and 'base.page_request.campaign' are the two mutually-exclusive referred new-session shapes the tracker emits: a referrer-inferred visit carries session_referer (and the server derives source/medium/referer from it), while a campaign-tagged visit (owa_* URL params) carries tagged_campaign/tagged_source/tagged_medium/tagged_terms/attribs INSTEAD of session_referer -- the tracker reports what the URL was TAGGED with and the server resolves campaign/source/medium/search_terms from it (the campaign attribution path suppresses referrer inference). These are captured by tests/js/BeaconContractReferred.test.js. 'base.page_request.customvars' is a new-session pageview carrying custom variables set via setCustomVar(slot,name,value,scope): each set slot rides the wire as a single 'cv{slot}' param whose value is the 'name=value' string (here slots 1-3 for page/session/visitor scope respectively); the server splits each into cv{slot}_name/cv{slot}_value. Captured by tests/js/BeaconContractCustomVars.test.js and ingested by tests/CustomVariableIngestionTest.php.
